questions.question: What is the primary strategy used in QuickSort algorithm?

explanations.a: Correct! QuickSort uses divide and conquer by partitioning the array around a pivot and recursively sorting the partitions.
explanations.b: Dynamic Programming is used for optimization problems with overlapping subproblems, not for QuickSort.
explanations.c: Greedy approach makes local optimal choices, which is not how QuickSort works.
explanations.d: Backtracking explores all possible solutions by undoing choices, which is not used in QuickSort.

questions.question: In QuickSort, what is the purpose of the pivot element?

answers.b: To divide the array into two partitions
answers.c: To count the number of elements

explanations.a: The pivot is not used to find the minimum element directly.
explanations.b: Correct! The pivot divides the array such that elements smaller than pivot go to one side and larger elements go to the other side.
explanations.c: The pivot is not used for counting elements.
explanations.d: The pivot is not used to find the maximum element directly.

questions.question: What is the best-case time complexity of QuickSort?

explanations.a: O(n) is too fast for a comparison-based sorting algorithm's best case.
explanations.b: Correct! When the pivot divides the array into equal halves at each step, we get O(n log n) time complexity.
explanations.c: O(n²) is the worst-case time complexity, not the best case.
explanations.d: O(log n) is not achievable for sorting n elements.

questions.question: Which of the following pivot selection strategies can help avoid worst-case performance?

explanations.a: Choosing the first element can lead to worst-case O(n²) performance on sorted arrays.
explanations.b: Choosing the last element can also lead to worst-case performance on certain inputs.
explanations.c: Correct! Random pivot selection helps achieve expected O(n log n) performance by avoiding consistently bad pivot choices.
explanations.d: Always choosing the middle element by position (not value) doesn't guarantee good performance.

questions.question: After one complete partitioning step in QuickSort, which statement is true about the pivot element?

answers.a: It might need to be moved again
answers.b: It is in its final sorted position
answers.c: It is the smallest element in the array
answers.d: It is the largest element in the array

explanations.a: Once partitioned correctly, the pivot doesn't need to be moved again.
explanations.b: Correct! After partitioning, the pivot is in its final sorted position with smaller elements to its left and larger elements to its right.
explanations.c: The pivot is not necessarily the smallest element, just in its correct sorted position.
explanations.d: The pivot is not necessarily the largest element, just in its correct sorted position.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort and when does it occur?

answers.a: O(n log n) when array is randomly ordered
answers.b: O(n²) when pivot is always the median
answers.c: O(n²) when pivot is always the smallest or largest element
answers.d: O(n) when array is already sorted

explanations.a: O(n log n) is actually the average case for randomly ordered arrays.
explanations.b: When pivot is the median, we get the best case O(n log n), not worst case.
explanations.c: Correct! Worst case O(n²) occurs when the pivot is always the smallest or largest element, creating highly unbalanced partitions.
explanations.d: O(n) is not achievable for comparison-based sorting of n elements.

questions.question: In the context of QuickSort, what does 'reducing the problem' mean?

answers.b: Dividing the array into smaller subarrays to sort independently
answers.d: Converting to a simpler sorting algorithm

explanations.a: While comparisons may be optimized, 'reducing' specifically refers to problem size reduction.
explanations.b: Correct! Reducing means breaking the original sorting problem into smaller independent sorting problems (partitions).
explanations.c: QuickSort doesn't specifically remove duplicates, though it handles them.
explanations.d: QuickSort doesn't convert to another algorithm; it reduces the problem size through partitioning.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of QuickSort in the average case?

explanations.a: O(1) would mean constant space, but QuickSort needs space for recursion stack.
explanations.b: Correct! The average case space complexity is O(log n) due to the recursion stack depth.
explanations.c: O(n) space would be needed in the worst case when recursion depth is maximum.
explanations.d: O(n log n) space is not required by QuickSort.
